minutes.headline: Open Space Committee voted to recommend the town use its right of first refusal on 250 Howard Street land.
minutes.summary: The committee welcomed two new members, set monthly third-Tuesday meetings through December, and elected a vice chair. It discussed transferring town-owned land to conservation or parks control, the economic development committee seat, and the Chapter 61B withdrawal at 250 Howard Street. It also voted to encourage town boards to seek a trail connection on the proposed greenhouse parcel.

budget_items.what_was_said: The purchase and sale agreement price the town would have to meet was stated, with a deposit and balance due at performance. The chair estimated a per-acre cost similar to the Seliba purchase.
The chair explained that Chapter 61 programs give owners property tax reductions, which cost the community revenue in exchange for the right of first refusal.
An appropriation by town meeting would be needed to exercise the right of first refusal.

The town-owned property disposition topic will return at the next meeting, with the parcel lists and maps pulled from the plan.
Members will individually seek candidates for the open space seat on the economic development committee and bring names to the next meeting.
Paula will forward the summarized recommendation to the chair, who will pass it to the board of selectmen before their September 8th meeting.
A member will raise the wrong open space plan link on the town website with the land use director.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee voted to recommend that the town pursue its right of first refusal on the 250 Howard Street land.
The committee voted to encourage the planning board and conservation commission to secure trail connectivity or an easement between two town parcels near the proposed greenhouse parcel.
The recommendation is to be forwarded to the chair and then to the board of selectmen ahead of their September 8th meeting.
Exercising the right would need an appropriation by town meeting, as explained in the discussion of the Chapter 61B withdrawal.
Members nominated Paula as vice chairperson, and meetings were set for the third Tuesday of each month at 6 p.m.

why_it_matters: If the town exercises the right of first refusal on 250 Howard Street, town meeting would be asked to vote an appropriation, which would draw on the town budget, mostly taxes.

Chapter 61 programs lower an owner's property taxes in exchange for the town's right of first refusal, so the vote touches both land the town could keep as open space and the revenue it gives up under the program.
watch_next: The board of selectmen meeting on September 8th, where the recommendation is due to be passed on.
The next committee meeting, which is to take up the list of town-owned parcels for possible conservation or parks control and candidates for the economic development committee seat.
